toegepas.rede_vinder: Used adverbially, the word group 'end aan end' is written as separate words without hyphens, like 'kop aan kop'.
toegepas.fout: The adverbial word group 'end aan end' is written as separate words in the AWS (like 'kop aan kop', 'hand aan hand'); hyphens belong only in attributive compounds.
toegepas.rede_keurder: A plain spelling fix inside the glossary entry that touches no protected wording and leaves the meaning exactly as it was.

laat_vaar.blok: Hoe jy 'n dier in die regte groep plaas
laat_vaar.voor: Moenie sy pote tel nie en moenie kyk
laat_vaar.na: Moenie sy pote tel nie, en moenie kyk
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Two complete imperative clauses, each with its own verb and negation, are joined by 'en'; a comma separates them and makes the double 'moenie ... nie' easier to read (borderline under the AWS rule, as imperatives have no stated subject).
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Two short subjectless imperatives sharing one 'moenie' frame read cleanly without a comma, and the AWS rule applies to clauses with their own subject, so the change is not required and adds nothing.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Ons verdeel hulle almal in twee groepe met net een enkele vraag.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Ons verdeel hulle almal met net een vraag in twee groepe.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'net een enkele' is redundant, and the means phrase reads more naturally before the result phrase.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The sentence already flows, and 'net een enkele' is a deliberate emphasis that the next sentence pays off, so dropping it and reordering is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Die slak bou daardie skulp self van kalk
laat_vaar_vorige.na: 'n Slak bou sy skulp self van kalk
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The previous sentence speaks of 'baie slakke', so 'die slak' and 'daardie skulp' have no single referent; a general 'n slak ... sy skulp' fits.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Die slak ... daardie skulp' ties back to the snails that carry a shell, whereas a general ''n Slak bou sy skulp' implies every snail has one and loses the 'baie' qualifier of the previous sentence.
